explanation: Each whole step on the scale is a tenfold change, so lemon juice, at about pH 2, is roughly 100,000 times more acidic than pure water at pH 7.

claims.text: The pH scale measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is.
pH does not measure saltiness, density or temperature.
Each whole unit on the pH scale is a tenfold change in acidity (in the concentration of hydrogen ions).
Lemon juice has a pH of about 2.
Pure water has a pH of 7 at 25 °C.
A solution at pH 2 is about 100,000 times more acidic than one at pH 7.
